ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is a small gecko with a snout-vent length of 60–70 mm. It features a brownish body with dark transverse bands and possesses distinct, strongly keeled subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal band and a series of 6–8 dark, wavy dorsal crossbands.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is endemic to the hillocks of Guwahati, Assam, where it inhabits moist deciduous forest patches and rocky outcrops at low elevations.
ai.behavior: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that remains hidden in rock crevices during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus guwahatiensis* is endemic to the hills of Guwahati in Assam, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 100 and 200 meters.
